title: Each memstore need has one route, and each rejection on the way names its fix
proves: a copy of every memstore row is a later generate with sourceEntity and the identifier/foreign-key role pair
a lookup in a data file is a variable with storage="data" and needs no memstore
a subset of rows is a nested generate with a braces count and an explicit max_count
a memstore that nothing reads back as a product is rejected, also when a variable reads it, and the remediation names the routes
a readback without the role pair or with fewer rows than the producer is rejected
max_count is the total of all rows: the total passes, the ceiling 2000 passes, one below the total, a missing max_count and 2001 are rejected
a count expression without braces and an interpolation token or __import__ in a script are rejected with the correct form

negatives.name: readback_replaced_by_generated_rows
negatives.remediation: A copy of every row: after teams add <generate name="teams_copy" source="mem" sourceEntity="teams"

patch.old:
<generate name="team_copy" source="mem" sourceEntity="teams" distribution="ordered">
        <key name="team_id" script="this.team_id"/>

negatives.name: variable_read_is_no_readback
negatives.remediation: a <variable source="mem"> read is not a readback

patch.old:
<generate name="team_copy" source="mem" sourceEntity="teams" distribution="ordered">
        <key name="team_id" script="this.team_id"/>
patch.new:
<generate name="team_copy" count="3">
        <variable name="team" source="mem" sourceEntity="teams" distribution="ordered"/>
        <key name="team_id" script="team.team_id"/>

negatives.name: readback_of_a_subset
negatives.remediation: a braces count there also needs "max_count" at the top level of acceptance/build.json

negatives.name: max_count_missing
negatives.remediation: add "max_count": <the rows of all products together> at the top level of acceptance/build.json

negatives.name: count_expression_without_braces
negatives.remediation: a Python expression in braces, count="{2 + 1}"

negatives.name: import_in_script
negatives.remediation: Scripts have no __import__; the datetime module is there

negatives.name: interpolation_in_script
negatives.remediation: Use the bare Python variable name in script, condition or where

patch.old: script="{row.person_id: row.tier for row in tiers}.get(str(person_id), 'NONE')"
patch.new: script="{row.person_id: row.tier for row in tiers}.get(str(__person_id__), 'NONE')"
